group.passage: Many of the games students play in PE class today did not simply appear. They were designed on purpose by teachers who needed something new for their classes. Two of the best-known team sports in the world, in fact, were born only four years apart in the same American state. Here are their stories.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: Basketball
passage_parts.text: In December 1891, James Naismith, a young physical education teacher at a YMCA training school in Springfield, Massachusetts, was facing a difficult class. The long New England winter had kept his students indoors for weeks. They were bored with the same old exercises they were required to do in the gym. His supervisor asked him to come up with a new game that could be played inside. Naismith borrowed ideas from soccer, rugby, and a children’s game called “duck on a rock.” For goals, he asked the janitor for two boxes, but the man returned with two peach baskets instead. Naismith had them nailed to the railing of a balcony ten feet above the gym floor, and an old soccer ball became the first basketball. Since the baskets still had their bottoms, the ball had to be taken out by hand after every score. The very first game turned so violent that Naismith realized he needed more rules.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: Volleyball
passage_parts.text: A few years later, a former student of the same Springfield school faced a different problem. William Morgan was teaching physical education at the YMCA in Holyoke, Massachusetts, where many of the members were businessmen. Morgan believed that basketball was too rough and tiring for these men. In 1895, at the Holyoke YMCA, he created a calmer game by combining parts of basketball with tennis and handball. Players hit a ball over a net that divided the two teams, and nobody had to crash into anybody else. Morgan named his new game “mintonette.” The next year, he showed the game to a group of visitors at the Springfield school. After watching the ball fly back and forth over the net, one of them suggested a better name: “volley ball.” The new name stuck, and the two words were later joined into one.

translation_zh.text:
今天學生在體育課玩的許多運動，並不是自然而然出現的，而是老師為了替班上找點新花樣而刻意設計出來的。事實上，世界上最知名的兩種團體運動，就誕生在美國同一個州，前後只相隔四年。以下是它們的故事。

A（籃球）1891 年 12 月，麻薩諸塞州春田市一所 YMCA（基督教青年會）訓練學校的年輕體育老師詹姆士‧奈史密斯，正面對一個棘手的班級。新英格蘭地區漫長的冬天，讓他的學生好幾週都只能待在室內。他們對體育館裡規定要做的那些一成不變的練習感到厭煩。他的主管要他想出一種可以在室內玩的新遊戲。奈史密斯借用了足球、橄欖球，以及一種叫做「石上鴨」的兒童遊戲的點子。至於球門，他向工友要兩個箱子，那人卻拿了兩個裝桃子的籃子回來。奈史密斯請人把籃子釘在離體育館地板十英尺高的看臺欄杆上，一顆舊足球就成了第一顆籃球。由於籃子還有底，每次得分後都得用手把球拿出來。第一場比賽打得非常粗暴，讓奈史密斯明白自己需要更多規則。

B（排球）幾年後，同一所春田學校的一位校友遇到了另一個問題。威廉‧摩根在麻薩諸塞州霍利奧克的 YMCA 教體育，那裡的會員很多是商人。摩根認為籃球對這些人來說太粗暴、太累人。1895 年，他在霍利奧克的 YMCA 把籃球、網球和手球的部分元素結合起來，創造出一種比較溫和的遊戲。球員把球打過一張隔開兩隊的網子，誰也不必撞上別人。摩根把這個新遊戲取名為「mintonette」。隔年，他在春田那所學校向一群來訪的人展示這個遊戲。看著球在網子兩邊來回飛，其中一人建議了一個更好的名字：「volley ball」（來回擊球）。新名字就此沿用下來，後來兩個字也合成了一個字（volleyball）。
